chunks.l2:
[tal-a14-v01] Now the nature of concealment, as it is told, let it be examined: from own nature the Supreme Lord touches the rule-bound and rule-free order.

[tal-a14-v10] Who on your teaching-path, initiated, falling through delusion into dissent: surely of them there is not your sun-appointment — can lotuses contract from sunbeams?

[tal-a14-v02] Touching, he shines forth; thereby he is called self-willed: having resorted to the rule of action and fruit — this Great Lord.

[tal-a14-v03] He ordains creation, preservation, destruction — the intermediate states; and again, in the great creation, in the endlessness of creation and destruction.

[tal-a14-v04] One, that God, universe-self, the Lord arrived at abandoning rule; and whatever intermediate creation — and stasis here too is unforced.

[tal-a14-v05] He does not abandon the form; niyati-abandoned, standing here: that. But by niyati alone, when, through the self-concealing procedure.

[tal-a14-v06] He enjoys suffering, delusion and the rest; then the action-fruit order — but having abandoned the karmic restraint, enveloped in suffering-delusion.

[tal-a14-v07] Desiring to shine forth, sits this one, in concealment disregardful; as from light's freedom, the awakened like the unawakened.

[tal-a14-v08] So sits, uncrossed yet as-if-crossed, behaving; as the awake one her fool-conduct performing even while hating it.

[tal-a14-v09] In the heart sits the fool — thus indeed of the awakened is the conduct; and the venerable Vidyā-lord said, in the Mānastotra, such as this.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-:C14 atha śrītantrāloke caturdaśamāhnikam tirobhāvasvarūpaṃ tu kathyamānaṃ vivicyatām / svabhāvāt parameśāno niyatyaniyatikramam spṛśanprakāśate yena tataḥ svacchanda ucyate / niyatiṃ karmaphalayorāśrityaiṣa maheśvaraḥ sṛṣṭisaṃsthitisaṃhārānvidhatte@vāntarasthitīn / mahāsarge punaḥ sṛṣṭisaṃhārānantyaśālini ekaḥ sa devo viśvātmā niyatityāgataḥ prabhuḥ / avāntare yā ca sṛṣṭiḥ sthitiścātrāpyayantritam nojjhatyeṣa vapustyaktaniyatiśca sthito@tra tat / niyatyaiva yadā caiṣa svarūpācchādanakramāt bhuṅkte duḥkhavimohādi tadā karmaphalakramaḥ / tyaktvā tu niyamaṃ kārmaṃ duḥkhamohaparītatām bibhāsayiṣurāste@yaṃ tirodhāne@napekṣakaḥ / yathā prakāśasvātantryāt pratibuddho@pyabuddhavat āste tadvadanuttīrṇo@pyuttīrṇa iva ceṣṭate / yathā ca buddhastāṃ mūḍhaceṣṭāṃ kurvannapi dviṣan hṛdyāste mūḍha evaṃ hi prabuddhānāṃ viceṣṭitam / śrīvidyādhipatiścāha mānastotre tadīdṛśam ye yauṣmāke śāsanamārge kṛtadīkṣāḥ saṃgacchanto mohavaśādvipratipattim / nūnaṃ teṣā nāsti bhavadbhānuniyogaḥ saṅkocaḥ kiṃ sūryakaraistāmarasānām

chunks.l2:
[tal-a14-v11] Known-and-knowable, standing in the creator's place though being, who going wrong from your path, they too are not right: mostly of them, arisen from emblem-mind-and-the-rest, false awakening like snake-fat lamplight.

[tal-a14-v12] Since pierced, with lead foremost: now copper — that which again to its own nature would not return; nor drunk by earth-dwellers, that nectar of whom thirst-hunger-suffering-pains again herein.

[tal-a14-v13] Then this awakened conduct — mantra-conduct-worship-and-the-rest: hate-kindled inwardly burns him; burning is doubt indeed — for.

[tal-a14-v14] Nor is it his past action's might, such that thereby thus he has come; indeed, what would that action be? Or why here would the procedure be the same as with the earlier?

[tal-a14-v15] Hence that, the Lord's will, by which deluded, so, endless-time-felt suffering-vesselhood he seeks.

[tal-a14-v16] There too, if through will-variety, both-here-and-beyond-natured: of suffering too there is division, made slow-or-swift, so.

[tal-a14-v17] Of Kāla, Kāma, Andhaka and the rest, of Paulastya-city dwellers, and of others: concealment — so much suffering, indeed hereafter too.

[tal-a14-v18] Another too is concealment, consisting in samaya-violation: which was said by the Lord in the venerable Ānandagahvara.

[tal-a14-v19] From samaya-violation, O Goddess: carrion-eaterhood for a hundred years; there too, through mild-intense-and-other-divisions, manifold is the course.

[tal-a14-v20] And through the Great Lord's freedom, though concealed, this one himself: through another's door, or comes back — again grace too, amply.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-jñātajñeyā dhātṛpadasthā api santo ye tvanmārgātkāpathagāste@pi na samyaka / prāyasteṣāṃ laiṅgikabuddhyādisamuttho mithyābodhaḥ sarpavasādīpajakalpaḥ yasmādviddhaṃ sūtakamukhyena nu tāmraṃ tadyadbhūyaḥ svāṃ prakṛtiṃ no samupeyāt / no taiḥ pītaṃ bhūtalasaṃsthairamṛtaṃ tadyeṣāṃ tṛṭkṣudduḥkhavibādhāḥ punarasmin tataḥ prabuddhaceṣṭāsau mantracaryārcanādikā / dveṣeddhāntardahatyenaṃ dāhaḥ śaṅkaiva sā yataḥ na cāsya karmamahimā tādṛgyenetthamāsta saḥ / kiṃ hi tatkarma kasmādvā pūrveṇātra samo vidhiḥ tasmātsā parameśecchā yayāyaṃ mohitastathā / anantakālasaṃvedyaduḥkhapātratvamīhate tatrāpi cecchāvaicitryādihāmutrobhayātmakaḥ / duḥkhasyāpi vibhedo@sti ciraśaighryakṛtastathā kālakāmāndhakādīnāṃ paulastyapuravāsinām / tathānyeṣāṃ tirobhāvastāvadduḥkho hyamutra ca anyo@pi ca tirobhāvaḥ samayollaṅghanātmakaḥ / yaduktaṃ parameśena śrīmadānandagahvare samayollaṅghanāddevi kravyādatvaṃ śataṃ samāḥ / tatrāpi mandatīvrādibhedādbahuvidhaḥ kramaḥ svātantryācca maheśasya tirobhūto@pyasau svayam / paradvāreṇa vābhyeti bhūyo@nugrahamapyalam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a14-v21] And from renewed grace, expiation-and-the-rest being performed: accordingly, in initiation and the rest performed, he would be Śiva-natured.

[tal-a14-v22] Concealed — even the departed-breathed: kin, friends, teachers having resorted to, through śaktipāta, through initiations is graced.

[tal-a14-v23] There too, diversity of quick-slow-time and the rest: so comes śaktipāta — it, by which he comes to Śiva-nature.

[tal-a14-v24] Thus creation, maintenance, dissolution, concealment, grace: in the five, doership is Śiva-hood, of consciousness-self.

[tal-a14-v25] Proud of five-act-freedom-complete-selfhood: the yogin's worship-japa-meditation-yogas, let them stand united, ever-risen.

[tal-a14-v26] In magic-show business one should never delight: even Sadāśiva — which enjoyment is bondage — that too, for the unfit.

[tal-a14-v27] Knowerness alone is Śiva-hood, is freedom: that is here called; like a potter, but, doership is not primary, from His superintendence.

[tal-a14-v28] Thus having known, to be grasped, never at all, ever, refutation: 'I am Śiva' — if following my will, why is not the world — thus the doubt.

[tal-a14-v29] 'Let them follow my will' — here in the I-knower, may it flash: Śiva, or the Supreme Lord — body and the rest, then, fashioned.

[tal-a14-v30] Of Śiva, for now is this — the body — but this, so fashioned by you: what other bodiness of his? Then what would be a speakable state?
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-bhūyo@nugrahataḥ prāyaścittādyācaraṇe sati / anusāreṇa dīkṣādau kṛte syācchivatāmayaḥ tirobhūtaḥ paretāsurapi bandhusuhṛdgurūn / ālambya śaktipātena dīkṣādyairanugṛhyate tatrāpi kālaśīghratvaciratvādivibhedatām / tathaiti śaktipāto@sau yenāyāti śivātmatām itthaṃ sṛṣṭisthitidhvaṃsatirobhāvamanugrahaḥ / iti pañcasu kartṛtvaṃ śivatvaṃ saṃvidātmanaḥ pañcakṛtyasvatantratvasaṃpūrṇasvātmamāninaḥ / yogino@rcājapadhyānayogāḥ saṃsyuḥ sadoditāḥ aindrajālikavṛttānte na rajyeta kadācana / sādāśivo@pi yo bhogo bandhaḥ so@pyucitātmanām jñātṛtvameva śivatā svātantryaṃ tadihocyate / kulālavattu kartṛtvaṃ na mukhyaṃ tadadhiṣṭhiteḥ iti jñātvā grahītavyā naiva jātvapi khaṇḍanā / śivo@haṃ cenmadicchānuvarti kiṃ na jagattviti mamecchāmanuvartantāmityatrāhaṃvidi sphuret / śivo vā parameśāno dehādiratha nirmitaḥ śivasya tāvadastyetaddehastveṣa tathā tvayā / kṛtaḥ kānyā dehatāsya tatkiṃ syādvācyatāpadam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a14-v31] Told, and, in the Siddhasantāna venerable Ūrmi-Mahākula: wind-wandering-breath-scattering-and-the-rest-made toilers.

[tal-a14-v32] In frauds and the rest, who deluded — they: deluded in the supreme state; everywhere with honor which even departure — for liberation.

[tal-a14-v33] Taught, she in the essence-śāstras, as enjoyment-means arisen: if all-pervading is God — tell! having departed, where will he go?

[tal-a14-v34] But if not all-pervading, then pot-like then he would be: the departure-rite-yoga — this partially — is taught.

[tal-a14-v35] In the partless Śiva-principle, but, how departure-fittingness? As from earth-and-the-rest to wind-end, by cliff-water-fire fasts.

[tal-a14-v36] Of the self joining in the void, likewise departure-procedure: therefore one should not make the soul depart out of longing for the supreme principle.

[tal-a14-v37] But in the venerable Pūrvaśāstra, whatever of departure the mark was told: not that, as a means to liberation, but for loss of enjoyment, from such desiring.

[tal-a14-v38] Perfected by japa-meditation-and-the-rest, through freedom, from śaktipāta: toward enjoyment detached, if thus: the body should abandon — quoted.

[tal-a14-v39] Even of self-willed death, what from Bhīṣma onward is heard, indeed: on arrival at enjoyment-distaste, approaching life's end.

[tal-a14-v40] By yoga-mantra-nectar-substance-boon-and-the-rest, a siddhi-partaking body: to abandon — for not otherwise is possible without the stated-sequence-practice.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-uktaṃ ca siddhasantānaśrīmadūrmimahākule / pavanabhramaṇaprāṇavikṣepādikṛtaśramāḥ kuhakādiṣu ye bhrāntāste bhrāntāḥ parame pade / sarvatra bahumānena yāpyutkrāntirvimuktaye proktā sā sāraśāstreṣu bhogopāyatayoditā / yadi sarvagatā devo vadotkramya kva yāsyati athāsarvagatastarhi ghaṭatulyastadā bhavet / utkrāntividhiyogo@yamekadeśena kathyate niraṃśe śivatattve tu kathamutkrāntisaṃgatiḥ / yathā dharādau vāyvante bhṛgvambvagnyupavāsakaiḥ ātmano yojanaṃ vyomni tadvadutkrāntivartanā / tasmānnotkramayejjīvaṃ paratattvasamīhayā śrīpūrvaśāstre tūktaṃ yadutkrānterlakṣaṇaṃ na tat / muktyupāyatayā kiṃtu bhogahānyai tathaiṣaṇāt japadhyānādisaṃsiddhaḥ svātantryācchaktipātataḥ / bhogaṃ prati viraktaśceditthaṃ dehaṃ tyajediti svacchandamṛtyorapi yad bhīṣmādeḥ śrūyate kila / bhogavairasyasaṃprāptau jīvitāntopasarpaṇam yogamantrāmṛtadravyavarādyaiḥ siddhibhāktanuḥ / hātuṃ nahyanyathā śakyā vinoktakramayogataḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a14-v41] Told, and, in the Mālinītantra, by the Supreme Lord, likewise: all — even, or else — enjoyment deeming ugly.

[tal-a14-v42] Thus-and-the-rest, by one who says: by all, the inner-reality-unseen reality, teaching of one's own freedom in creation-and-the-rest duties.

[tal-a14-v43] Which very chief initiation should be of the disciple, Śiva-giving: told in the venerable Niśicāra, and by Bhairavī energy, radiance.

[tal-a14-v44] Pervaded, the universe they behold, the thought-abandoned-minded; but the thought-joined-minded: from body's fall, Śiva reaches.

[tal-a14-v45] By outer-initiation-and-the-rest-practice, through conduct-samaya-constructs, thought-free just so now indeed: living-liberated, no doubt.

[tal-a14-v46] By thought made like the root-mass of the world-worn-out tree, inwardly, of the ultimate fire: may there be spark-fragments; even if at its end, blazes intensely the pure-awakening-fire-mass.

[tal-a14-v47] Thus the initiation-approach — this, shown, scripturally approved.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-uktaṃ ca mālinītantre parameśena tādṛśam / sarvamapyathavā bhogaṃ manyamāno virūpakam ityādi vadatā sarvairalakṣyāntaḥsatattvakam / evaṃ sṛṣṭyādikartavyasvasvātantryopadeśanam yatsaiva mukhyadīkṣā syācchiṣyasya śivadāyinī / uktaṃ śrīniśicāre ca bhairavīyeṇa tejasā vyāptaṃ viśvaṃ prapaśyanti vikalpojjhitacetasaḥ / vikalpayuktacittastu piṇḍapātācchivaṃ vrajet bāhyadīkṣādiyogena caryāsamayakalpanaiḥ / avikalpastathādyaiva jīvanmukto na saṃśayaḥ saṃsārajīrṇatarumūlakalāpakalpasaṃkalpasāntaratayā paramārthavahneḥ / syurvisphuliṅgakaṇikā api cettadante dedīpyate vimalabodhahutāśarāśiḥ itthaṃ dīkṣopakramo@yaṃ darśitaḥ śāstrasaṃmataḥ / [AbhT_14.47]
